gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: It ___ no difference whether we leave today or tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Make no difference' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: The wedding will ___ place in the village church.
gaps.explanation: take place means to happen; it is the fixed phrase for events.

gaps.sentence: Who will ___ responsibility for the project now that Jane has left?
gaps.explanation: take responsibility for something means to accept the duty of dealing with it.

gaps.sentence: All candidates must ___ the written exam in June.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'exam' from the candidate's side
gaps.explanation: take an exam (or sit an exam) means to be tested; 'give an exam' is not used in British English.

gaps.sentence: I'm ___ a course in web design this term.
gaps.explanation: do a course is the British English collocation for studying on a course.
